intro: On the Euphrates, in Gaziantep province, lies Zeugma, an ancient city dating from 300 BC. This is the city of villa mosaics, and the home of the famous 'Gypsy Girl'.
history: Seleucus I founded the city at a crossing of the Euphrates, and it later became a Roman legionary base. Its extraordinary mosaics were rescued before the Birecik dam flooded the site.
structure-4: And now to the Zeugma Mosaic Museum, which houses one of the world's richest mosaic collections.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the villa mosaics, the Roman houses and the rock tombs.
facts: Did you know? The 'Gypsy Girl' mosaic is displayed in the world's largest mosaic museum. The city's name is Greek for 'crossing': this was the easiest ford on the Euphrates, and the lock on the eastern trade. Among the mosaics saved in the rescue dig before the Birecik dam flooded the site is the 'Gypsy Girl', now one of the best-known ancient images in Türkiye. And Rome's Legio IV Scythica was stationed here; the city's wealth came directly from the frontier garrison.
outro: This brings our journey through Zeugma to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
